articles.title: Is Kyle Tucker a $240M mistake? Dave Roberts addresses Dodgers star's alarming slump
articles.standfirst: Kyle Tucker was supposed to be the missing piece for the Dodgers. Instead, his struggles have raised major concerns in Los Angeles.
articles.summary: Kyle Tucker was supposed to be the missing piece for the Dodgers. Instead, his struggles have raised major concerns in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
The massive investment the Los Angeles Dodgers made in Kyle Tucker has not been fully reflected in his performance, as he has fallen far short of expectations.

Tucker, who signed a contract that made him the player with the highest true average annual value in MLB history , has not lived up to the enormous expectations surrounding his arrival in Los Angeles. His 0.1 WAR is the worst mark of his career since his rookie season, while his defensive struggles have become a growing concern as his bat continues to remain cold.

Dave Roberts backs Kyle Tucker amid Dodgers struggles

During an appearance on MLB Network Radio , manager Dave Roberts defended his right fielder and made it clear that he believes Tucker can overcome this difficult stretch.

“I think that it's one of those things I think for me is my message to him is you're not alone. But when you can you catch a ball at your shoe tops and drop it, that's where you're kind of that's a tell where you're not in a good spot mentally. You know, people miss fly balls all the time. It happens. Shouldn't happen, but it does,” Roberts said.

The Dodgers manager explained that he has also noticed some lack of confidence in Tucker’s at-bats.

“But when you're catching it that low, it's just kind of you're really unsure, right. The at-bats of kind of the indecisiveness, and I think for me is just wanting him to just kind of go out there and expect good things to happen. Go play free and easy.

“You're not gonna, you know, have a 900 this year, but you know each day just go out there and help us win the game. And I think that when you start just playing just to win and take the individual performance out of it hopefully that kind of alleviates some kind of angst and some frustrations. But yeah, I mean he's probably never struggled like this in his life.”

The Dodgers expected Tucker to be the definitive solution to their search for a consistent right fielder. After rotating players such as Jason Heyward , Kevin Kiermaier , and Michael Conforto at the position, the organization made a major investment in the former Chicago Cubs outfielder to fill that void.

However, so far, Tucker has the lowest WAR among Los Angeles’ regular starters, while his backup Alex Call has performed at a better level in fewer opportunities.

Despite the difficult adjustment, Roberts and the Dodgers continue to support the 2 9-year-old player , believing he can return to the level that made him one of MLB’s biggest stars .

articles.title: Is Mark Walter forced to sell the Dodgers? Bill Simmons makes shocking prediction
articles.standfirst: After selling the Lakers, Mark Walter’s Dodgers future is now under the spotlight.
articles.summary: After selling the Lakers, Mark Walter’s Dodgers future is now under the spotlight.
articles.body:
Journalist and analyst Bill Simmons believes the Los Angeles Dodgers could be the next major asset owned by billionaire Mark Walter to hit the market, following the record-breaking $12.5 billion sale of the Los Angeles Lakers and amid growing scrutiny surrounding his business empire.

During the latest episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast , Simmons discussed Walter’s situation, pointing to the Lakers sale and reports that the businessman is negotiating the sale of his stake in Chelsea FC . The commentator also speculated on the potential outcome of the federal investigation involving Walter and his businesses.

“It’s starting to seem like he might actually go to jail. He’s already shed himself of the Lakers. He’s selling his Chelsea stake reportedly right now, which was like 12.5%, and my guess is that the Dodgers are going to be next,” Simmons said. “So, what is this? Are we moving toward a Bernie Madoff, Ivan Boesky-type situation? Will the words ‘Mark Walter today pled guilty’ be said in the next two years?”

Walter has not been charged with any crime , meaning Simmons’ comments are purely speculation about where the ongoing federal investigation could ultimately lead.

Federal prosecutors and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) have been investigating potential financial irregularities involving Walter’s business interests. As part of the investigation, federal agents reportedly previously seized the businessman’s phones and computers, while two insurance companies under his control received grand jury subpoenas in February.

Simmons believes Walter’s entire sports empire could be at risk

Sam Koppelman , who joined Simmons during the discussion, agreed that Walter’s sports holdings could potentially be on the table.

“I think it’s really possible,” Koppelman said. “I also think the Trump administration has not put away very many billionaires and so I’m sure they work something out. But I don’t think there’s a single safe asset in the entire Mark Walter cinematic universe. Like, I think it’s potentially all for sale and I do think that the Dodgers being sold — I think all of this is on the table.”

A Dodgers sale would have massive MLB implications

Walter’s potential departure from the Dodgers would have a major impact across Major League Baseball. The businessman has been the team’s controlling owner and chairman since Guggenheim Baseball Management acquired the franchise in 2012 .

“That’s why it’s such a bigger story than just the Lakers,” Simmons said. “If he has to sell the Dodgers, who spent so much money over the last seven years that they’re going to single-handedly create the baseball lockout next year. They also won two titles. He’s had all this extra money to buy the last two World Series titles. The Dodgers are back-to-back champions partly because of all the f***ing money this guy spent.”

Under Walter’s ownership, Los Angeles has become one of baseball’s most dominant organizations, combining aggressive spending with consistent regular-season success. The Dodgers have won three World Series championships during his tenure, including back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025 .

For now, there is no confirmed agreement for Walter to sell the Dodgers . However, Simmons’ comments have once again raised questions about the future of the businessman’s sports portfolio as the federal investigation continues.

On the field, the Dodgers remain focused on pursuing a third consecutive championship. Los Angeles leads the National League West with a 76-51 record, ahead of the San Diego Padres (68-59), as the postseason approaches.

articles.title: Roki Sasaki has been on fire since major change - and it has nothing to do with Tarik Skubal or Shohei Ohtani
articles.standfirst: The Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher has turned around his 2026 season at the perfect time.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher has turned around his 2026 season at the perfect time.
articles.body:
Heading into the MLB Trade Deadline , there was only one question mark surrounding the Los Angeles Dodgers : Was their starting pitching rotation going to hold up until and through the postseason?

The front office clearly had those doubts, as they pulled off a big trade for Tarik Skubal . With Shohei Ohtani an unknown - on the mound - going forward, no one was quite sure what the rotation was going to look like. Blake Snell has now returned from injury, and Tyler Glasnow is getting closer to a return of his own. Yet it might be Roki Sasaki who's been the biggest benefactor of all of this chaos.

Since the All-Star break, Sasaki has been on a tear. Over his last six starts, he's given up just nine earned runs over 34.3 innings, while punching out nearly one batter per inning . In fact, two of those earned runs should probably have been unearned due to a poor route taken by Teoscar Hernandez in Sasaki's most recent start.

Roki Sasaki seems to have stopped tipping pitches since switching to larger glove

Regardless, Sasaki has figured things out at the perfect time for the Dodgers. As it turns out, Sasaki's big change to turn around his season had nothing to do with the other pitchers coming and going from the rotation: Instead, it's been using a large glove in order to keep him from tipping pitches .

The Dodgers' pitching coaches implored Sasaki to make the switch to a different glove, and the results speak for themselves. Now, the Dodgers are almost fully ready for the postseason; they just need Ohtani to get back on the mound, too .
